primary.title: Long Walk to Freedom
primary.author: Nelson Mandela
primary.rationale: Mandela's autobiography, providing a comprehensive account of his life, political activism, and imprisonment. It is a foundational primary source for understanding his personal journey and motivations.

primary.title: No Easy Walk to Freedom: Speeches, Articles and Broadcasts on the African Struggle
primary.author: Nelson Mandela
primary.rationale: A collection of Mandela's writings and speeches from the period of his active political leadership and prior to his long imprisonment. This offers direct insight into his political thought and strategy.

primary.title: The Struggle Is My Life
primary.author: Nelson Mandela
primary.rationale: Another collection of Mandela's writings and speeches, offering further primary evidence of his views and the anti-apartheid movement's objectives.

secondary.title: Mandela: An Autobiography
secondary.author: Nelson Mandela
secondary.rationale: While the autobiography itself is a primary source, scholarly analyses and critical editions of it are invaluable secondary sources. This entry refers to scholarly works that analyze the autobiography.

secondary.title: Nelson Mandela: The Authorized Biography
secondary.author: Anthony Sampson
secondary.rationale: Written by a journalist who knew Mandela for decades, this biography is considered a highly authoritative secondary source, drawing on extensive interviews and research.

secondary.title: Madiba: The Life and Times of Nelson Mandela
secondary.author: Martin Meredith
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive and well-regarded biography that synthesizes a vast amount of information about Mandela's life and the political context in which he operated.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources are generally autobiographical works or collections of speeches and writings. Secondary sources are scholarly biographies that provide historical context and analysis. Availability on Wikisource and Project Gutenberg for these specific primary source collections might be limited, with Internet Archive being the most probable repository.
